title: Density formula for the averaged indicator
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, let $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sin u\ne0$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[
u_u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^n p_{\sin^2 u}(\cos u\,x_i,z_i)\right)1_A(z)\,dz,
\]
where $u_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and $p_v(c,z)$ is the density at $z$ of a Gaussian random variable with mean $c$ and variance $v$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\prod_i p_{\sin^2u}(\cos u\,x_i,z_i)1_A(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(c,z)$ is the $N(c,v)$ density.
